subject.title: [Feature Request]: Native Prompt Caching Support for Amazon Nova (Bedrock)

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally change direct Amazon Bedrock Nova models from forced no-cache to native cache-point eligible behavior once live Nova proof is attached?
rationale: Source proves the requested behavior is missing, but enabling Nova prompt caching changes provider request shaping and default runtime behavior for existing Nova users.

options.title: Land the linked provider fix after live proof
options.body: Require redacted Nova Converse or ConverseStream proof, then accept the provider-owned cache policy change in the linked PR or a narrow replacement.

options.title: Require opt-in Nova caching
options.body: Preserve forced no-cache as the upgrade default and allow Nova cache points only through an explicit configuration or narrower policy gate.

options.title: Defer Nova native caching
options.body: Leave the current no-cache behavior in place until provider ownership or live AWS evidence makes the behavior change less uncertain.

recommendation.title: Land the linked provider fix after live proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted Nova Converse or ConverseStream proof, then accept the provider-owned cache policy change in the linked PR or a narrow replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Bedrock prompt-cache and provider-history signals make this the strongest available routing candidate for the behavior decision.
